skill.name: decision-mapping
skill.description: Turn a loose idea into a sequenced map of investigation tickets, then drive them to resolution one at a time.
skill.summary: Create and maintain compact decision maps for multi-session planning work.
skill.author: mattpocock

content.user_title: Map Complex Decisions Into Investigation Tickets
content.value_statement: Complex planning work often stalls when open decisions mix with implementation tasks. This skill turns uncertainty into compact tickets and guides each session to resolution.
actual_capabilities: Creates a compact Markdown decision map for one planning effort.
Structures entries as numbered tickets with dependencies, type, question, and answer.
Supports bootstrap sessions from loose ideas.
Supports resume sessions for a specified map path and ticket number.
Classifies tickets as Research, Prototype, or Grilling.
Updates the map when decisions reveal new tickets or invalidate old nodes.
limitations: Does not resolve tickets during the initial map-building session.
Depends on other skills for prototyping, grilling, and domain modeling.
Requires the full decision map to remain compact enough for session context.
Does not replace user judgment when deciding parallel work order.

use_cases.title: Plan Ambiguous Product Work
use_cases.description: Turn a broad product idea into ordered questions, research tasks, and clear decision points.

use_cases.title: Resolve Architecture Choices
use_cases.description: Break architecture uncertainty into research, prototype, and discussion tickets with dependency tracking.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Long Investigations
use_cases.description: Maintain a compact map when multiple sessions or agents must push related decisions forward.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Decision Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use decision-mapping for this idea: [brief idea]. Ask one question at a time and create the first map.

prompt_templates.title: Resume One Ticket
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue work from an existing map.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use decision-mapping with [map path] and ticket #[number]. Load the full map, resolve only this ticket, then update the map.

prompt_templates.title: Map Architecture Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use decision-mapping to map unresolved architecture choices for [project]. Separate research, prototype, and grilling tickets with dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Investigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare work for multiple agents or sessions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use decision-mapping to review [map path], identify tickets that can run in parallel, and preserve blocked_by dependencies.

output_examples.input: A team needs to choose a database for a new analytics product.
output_examples.output: A decision map with tickets for data shape, query needs, migration risk, prototype scope, and final database selection.

output_examples.input: An existing map has ticket 4 open about authentication provider choice.
output_examples.output: A resolved ticket summary with the decision, supporting evidence, and new follow-up tickets for integration risks.

output_examples.input: A project has too many unclear roadmap questions for one session.
output_examples.output: A compact sequence of research and discussion tickets that keeps unresolved work visible without duplicating assets.

best_practices: Keep each ticket small enough for one 100K token session.
Link assets from the map instead of copying full artifacts into it.
Resolve tickets in dependency order unless the map clearly supports parallel work.
anti_patterns: Using the map for simple tasks with no unresolved decisions.
Resolving tickets during the initial bootstrap session.
Duplicating large research notes inside the decision map.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a compact Markdown decision map with numbered tickets and dependency information.

faq.question: Can it work with existing maps?
faq.answer: Yes. Resume mode loads the full map and resolves one specified ticket at a time.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: Its main output is planning structure. Prototype tickets may use another skill to explore code or interface behavior.

faq.question: Where should the decision map live?
faq.answer: The skill expects one Markdown file per planning effort, tracked alongside the project.

faq.question: When should I skip the decision map?
faq.answer: Skip it when the initial discussion leaves no unresolved decisions or planning uncertainty.

faq.question: Can tickets run in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. Parallel work is possible when dependency edges show that tickets do not block each other.
